comments.value: This would be very useful for avatars that could have two different modes of visemes, such as crocodile that has normal visemes but then has ones that are swapped to be more constrained once duck tape is wrapped around their snout.
Didn't realize there was an existing canny here. Additional discussion is in https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/provide-individual-viseme-levels-as-avatar-float-parameters .

Cross-linking this to a different request, since both are related to how VRChat utilizes OVRLipSync  (Where VRChat gets the viseme data from), to additionally expose the Laughter Detection / LaughterProbability value also available in the newer versions of OVRLipSync

https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/laughter-detection

details:
If you use Blendshape driven visemes, you currently can't accurately reproduce the same result by manually implementing it; you can approximate it by utilizing `Voice` float in combination with the `Viseme` int, but the actual viseme system seems to be handling things differently.
It'd be nice to be able to get access to this data so you could recreate the entire system, manually if you wanted.
title: Expose Viseme Floats
